_comment: Cross-week checkpoint provenance manifest. Every SHA-256 here was COMPUTED from the local bytes with `shasum -a 256`, not read from a cache filename or an upstream etag -- see _why_computed below. This file is the durable record; it is small, committed, and is what makes a deleted checkpoint recognisable if it is ever re-obtained. It is NOT preservation: a hash identifies an artifact, it does not recreate one. See `source_durability` per entry.
_why_computed: During Phase 3B the Hugging Face download of any4d_4v_combined.pth reported etag 3d0590be06f0a1ca676fafccd829d2b51a969812b73726fb70e798307c9f4577, while the SHA-256 of the received bytes is e78d2ef25f506d262b8b70383a142373940f8c65754e95c4bda6b87d4d06ed85. Xet-backed repositories content-address differently from plain LFS, so an upstream-supplied identifier is not interchangeable with a SHA-256. Blob filenames in the local HF cache did match the computed SHA-256 for the three LFS-backed models below, but that is cache implementation detail and is deliberately not relied on.

_source_durability_scale.durable: public, versioned, content-addressed host with a resolved revision recorded (e.g. a Hugging Face repo at a pinned commit). A hash plus the revision is normally enough to re-obtain and verify the identical artifact.
_source_durability_scale.fragile: a link that can rot or be silently replaced with no version history (OneDrive, Google Drive, a personal URL). A hash can VERIFY a recovered file but cannot recover one. Deleting these trades rerunnability for space.
_source_durability_scale.transitive: pulled automatically by another package's code path; durability follows that upstream.

_retention_tiers.current_pipeline: in active use by the selected architecture -- keep locally; deleting only creates re-download friction
_retention_tiers.relevant_comparison: a serious challenger that may be wanted for a later sanity check or against C2 -- keep while the phase is fresh
_retention_tiers.closed_candidate: branch closed by a recorded decision; not part of the architecture and not scheduled to re-run -- delete after provenance harvest
_retention_tiers.deleted: already removed; retained here as a record only

checkpoints.method: MapAnything (Week 3 configuration D -- SELECTED dense range supplier)
checkpoints.checkpoint_license: Apache-2.0 (deliberately chosen over the default facebook/map-anything, which is CC-BY-NC-4.0)
checkpoints.note: Weeks 5-6 consume this model's range product. Also note that Week 3 established all three dense models are BITWISE reproducible, so keeping this checkpoint is what makes the derived range arrays disposable -- regenerating them is exactly equivalent to having kept them.

checkpoints.method: VGGT (Week 3 configuration E0 -- the paired control that makes Wat3R-Ren interpretable)
checkpoints.code_license: permits commercial use except military applications (2025-07-29 update)
checkpoints.checkpoint_license: NON-COMMERCIAL. The commercial VGGT-1B-Commercial variant is gated behind an application that was not made. E0 is an experimental control only and must not become a permanent project dependency.
checkpoints.note: Phase 3B found this the strongest arm on wreck_03 (4.0 % median vs A). Worth keeping while Week 3 is fresh and until C2, despite being licence-blocked as a default.

checkpoints.method: Wat3R-Ren (Week 3 configuration E -- underwater domain adaptation of VGGT)
checkpoints.note: Phase 3A: 'Wat3R-Ren remains a legitimate candidate with a condition-dependent adaptation effect' -- explicitly NOT established as inferior. Fully Apache-2.0, so unlike E0 it could be promoted. Keep.

checkpoints.resolved_checkpoint_revision: not pinned at download (fetched by direct resolve/main URL, not by revision)
checkpoints.checkpoint_license: NOT STATED -- the Hugging Face repo declares no license field and carries no licence file. A public artifact with no stated terms is not an open-source licence.
checkpoints.note: Classified interesting_but_not_material. Not part of the architecture and not scheduled to re-run. Largest single artifact in the project at 7.73 GB. NOTE the resolved revision was not captured at download time -- re-obtaining gives whatever is at resolve/main then, and only the SHA-256 above would reveal a substitution.

checkpoints.method: DINOv2 ViT-L/14 (encoder weights pulled by Any4D's model construction)
checkpoints.note: Reached only through Any4D's encoder construction; nothing else in the project uses it. Its own weights are then overwritten by the Any4D checkpoint. Deletable together with Any4D. Unversioned URL, so the SHA-256 is the only identity anchor.

checkpoints.method: Water-VGGT advertised geometry checkpoint (Week 3 configuration I -- release_incomplete)
checkpoints.checkpoint_repository: OneDrive link in the repository README
checkpoints.sha256: d15bf50a...3afe0 (TRUNCATED IN THE PHASE 3A RECORD -- see note)
checkpoints.local_path: DELETED -- no file matching it exists on this machine
checkpoints.note: THE EXEMPLAR CASE, and it cuts both ways. Deleting it was fine for the SCIENTIFIC RESULT: Phase 3A recorded that its model state is bitwise identical tensor-for-tensor to facebook/VGGT-1B (1797/1797 tensors, 0 key differences, max abs difference exactly 0.0), and that finding stands without the bytes. But the artifact INSPECTION is no longer independently rerunnable: the source is a OneDrive link with no version history, and the Phase 3A record stores the SHA-256 only in truncated display form (d15bf50a...3afe0), so even a recovered file could not be fully verified against it. Two lessons, both applied above: record full hashes, not elided ones; and treat fragile sources as the one class where a hash is not a substitute for the bytes.

checkpoints.method: SEA-RAFT-M (Week 2A -- CANONICAL correspondence backend, frozen by Phase 2B)
checkpoints.note: The frozen backend for every temporal metric in the project. KEEP. Only 79 MB, durable source, revision pinned and hash computed -- the cheapest insurance in the manifest.

checkpoints.source_identifier: Google Drive link from the WAFT README
checkpoints.note: Closed by the Phase 2A/2B selection, but the source is a Google Drive link -- deleting trades rerunnability for 245 MB. Small enough that keeping it is nearly free.

checkpoints.source_identifier: Google Drive link from the FlowIt README
checkpoints.note: Dropped in Phase 2A for non-reproducibility -- the precedent Week 3 cites when disqualifying a non-deterministic instrument. The decision rests on the recorded result, not on the weights.

checkpoints.source_identifier: Google Drive link from the VideoFlow README
checkpoints.note: 52 MB. Too small for deletion to be worth the loss of rerunnability.

_gaps: CLOSED 2026-09-01: SEA-RAFT-M revision, size and SHA-256 have now been computed and recorded.
Any4D and DINOv2: no resolved upstream revision was captured at download time -- both were fetched by unversioned direct URL. The SHA-256 is their only identity anchor.
Water-VGGT: the Phase 3A record stores its SHA-256 only in truncated display form, so the deleted artifact could not be fully verified even if recovered.
Week 2A entries have no recorded retrieval timestamp beyond 'Week 2A'.
